```{r setup, include=FALSE}

library(pcaLab)
```

## Matrix decomposition target

Principal Component Pursuit decomposes

$$X=L+S$$

where $L$ is low rank and $S$ is sparse. A common convex formulation is

$$\min_{L,S}\|L\|_*+\lambda\|S\|_1\quad\text{subject to }X=L+S.$$

`pcaLab` implements an inexact augmented-Lagrangian/SVT solver.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
L <- matrix(rnorm(120),40,3) %*% matrix(rnorm(30),3,10)
S <- matrix(0,40,10); S[sample(length(S),12)] <- rnorm(12,12,2)
fit <- pca_fit(L+S,method="rpca",center=FALSE,scale=FALSE,ncomp=3,max_iter=500)
fit$extra$converged
sqrt(mean(((L+S)-fit$extra$low_rank-fit$extra$sparse)^2))
```

PCA is then applied to the recovered low-rank matrix. This engine should be interpreted as matrix decomposition followed by PCA, not as ROBPCA.
